precepts.text: Righteousness is when we observe to do all these commandments.
precepts.point: Righteousness is defined by keeping the commandments.

note.label: Psalm 15: Who Shall Abide in the Tabernacle

precepts.why: “Lord, who shall abide in thy tabernacle? who shall dwell in thy holy hill?” The answer is the man that walketh uprightly and worketh righteousness and speaketh the truth in his heart. Righteousness is defined by keeping the commandments: “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” To work righteousness is to observe to do all these commandments.

precepts.text: The just man that doeth that which is lawful and right is the picture of this righteous cell.
precepts.point: These attributes are the same standard laid out in the law and in the description of the just, righteous man.

note.label: Psalm 15: Who Shall Abide in the Tabernacle

precepts.why:
“But if a man be just, and do that which is lawful and right”. The just man that doeth that which is lawful and right is the picture of this righteous man: one who backbiteth not with his tongue, does no evil to his neighbour, takes up no reproach against him, contemns the vile person but honours them that fear the Lord, sweareth to his own hurt and changeth not, puts not out his money to usury nor takes reward against the innocent.

These attributes are the same standard laid out in the law and in the description of the just, righteous man. “He that doeth these things shall never be moved.”

moments.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

points: Lord, who shall abide in thy tabernacle? Who shall dwell in thy holy hill? He that walketh uprightly, and worketh righteousness: that worketh is an action; you are putting your hand to the plow.

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

points: And speaketh the truth in his heart: that means he is the same all the time; he shows the integrity behind his thoughts.

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

points: He that backbiteth not with his tongue, nor doeth evil to his neighbour: a person working toward righteousness is not going to do evil to his neighbor, because he has great moral character. He honoureth them that fear the Lord; he that sweareth to his own hurt, and changeth not. He that doeth these things shall never be moved.

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

points: A, getting defensive: people do not like being told they are wrong, but how can you fix something if you are never corrected? B, talking about them afterward: taking the correction to the face, then going behind his back to minimize it as if the brother was out of the spirit. D, leaving emotionally: you have no emotional strength to deal with correction; that is that 2018 spirit; you cannot take it.

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

points: The Psalm opens with a question: who shall abide in the Most High's tabernacle and dwell in his holy hill. The answer is the man that walketh uprightly and worketh righteousness and speaketh the truth in his heart.

note.label: Psalm 15: Who Shall Abide in the Tabernacle

points: The righteous man does no evil to his neighbor, does not take up a reproach against him, condemns the vile person but honors them that fear the Lord, and sweareth to his own hurt and changeth not.

note.label: Psalm 15: Who Shall Abide in the Tabernacle

points: He puts not out his money to usury nor takes reward against the innocent. He that doeth these things shall never be moved.
These attributes are the same standard laid out in the law and in the description of the just, righteous man.
